lines: An FFT freeze: it holds the spectrum of what is coming in at the moment you freeze it and plays that back as a sustained pad, and passes the input through untouched the rest of the time
Freezes the spectrum and holds it; on the Toggle setting each press switches the freeze on or off, and on the Momentary setting the freeze lasts only while the button is held
Sets how much of the frozen spectrum is heard against the dry input, and is read only while the freeze is on, so with the freeze off the output is the input alone
Sets the length of the analysis window, from 128 samples up to about one second; with a clock at CLK it instead snaps to note lengths from a sixty-fourth up to a whole note
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the WINDOW input before it is added to the WINDOW knob
Sets how far the analysis frames overlap, a hop of half the window at the counter-clockwise end and an eighth of it at the clockwise end, which smears the sound across time
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the SHAPE input before it is added to the SHAPE knob
Reads the clock as straight, triplet or dotted note lengths, which changes the set of window lengths the WINDOW knob can reach
Sets how long the analysis window takes to move to a new length, from an immediate jump at the counter-clockwise end to one whole window length at the clockwise end
The left audio input, and the signal the right channel uses as well while IN R is empty
The right audio input; with nothing patched here it takes whatever is at IN L
Freezes the spectrum: on the Toggle setting each rising edge above 1V switches the freeze on or off, and on the Momentary setting the freeze holds while this reads above 0.1V
Moves the analysis window length, scaled by its attenuverter, with 5V covering the whole of the WINDOW knob's travel
Moves the frame overlap, scaled by its attenuverter, with 5V covering the whole of the SHAPE knob's travel
A clock here makes the window lengths note values of that clock; the rate is taken from the time between rising edges above 1V
The left output: the left input while the freeze is off, and that input mixed with the frozen spectrum while it is on
The right output: the right input while the freeze is off, and that input mixed with the frozen spectrum while it is on
Note — nothing is held until the freeze is switched on, by the button or by a gate at the FREEZE input; until then the module passes its input straight through and the MIX knob does nothing
Note — the display draws the spectrum the module is analysing
Menu — Freeze behavior: Momentary (hold gate), Toggle (on/off) — chooses whether the button and the gate hold the freeze while they are down or switch it on and off; the module starts on Toggle
Menu — Clock rate: 1 PPQ (1/4 note), 2 PPQ (1/8 note), 4 PPQ (1/16 note), 24 PPQ — tells the module how many pulses the clock sends per beat, which sets what the window lengths are measured against

FFTF.notes: Closed source; everything here was read from the installed 2.0.0 binary. The window length is resolved by resolveWindowN at 0x1108: free-running it is 128 samples at the counter-clockwise end rising to capN, which is the sample rate times 1.024 capped at 262144, so about one second; clocked it is chosen from the beat divided by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64, with any candidate under 128 samples or over the cap dropped. Clock division multiplies the beat by 2/3 for Triplet and 1.5 for Dotted. Shape sets the analysis hop to half the window times 2 to the power of minus twice the knob. The dry/wet mix is slewed towards its target at 50 per second and is forced to zero whenever the freeze is off, so an unfrozen FFTF is a straight wire. Nothing in the plugin reads a channel count, so every port is mono. The panel menu also carries Reload panel and Poll SVG for reload, which every module in this plugin has and which only reload the panel artwork; they are left out.

ModalFilter.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.0.0 binary. The frequency base is 20 times 900 to the power of the cutoff knob, giving 20Hz to 18000Hz, but ModalFilter::process at 0x1b804 tests whether the 1V/oct jack is connected and, when it is, replaces that base with 261.6256Hz and never reads the knob again, so a patched cable sitting at 0V pins the filter to C4. Resonance is 0.5 times 30 to the power of the knob and decay is 0.05 times 100 to the power of the knob. The nine model names are literals in the binary at 0x3a8ef: Harmonic string, Odd-harmonic tube, Stiff string, Tuned bar, Free-free bar, Circular membrane, Square membrane, Bell and Plate / cymbal; the ninth is shortened to plate on its line to keep it inside the line length, and the model knob fades between neighbouring pairs, which the tooltip shows as one name, an arrow, the next name and a percentage. The expander is found through the right-hand expander slot at Module+0x110 and its model is checked, so only a Modal Filter Expander counts and only on the right. Nothing in the plugin reads a channel count, so every port is mono; the maker's description of the expander as adding polyphonic voices means several resonators, not Rack polyphony. The panel menu also carries Reload panel and Poll SVG for reload, which every module in this plugin has and which only reload the panel artwork; they are left out.

ModalFilterExpander.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.0.0 binary. ModalFilterExpander::process at 0x21708 looks at the left-hand expander slot at Module+0xe8 and checks that the neighbour's model is Modal Filter, so the module is inert anywhere else. Each voice offset runs minus 1 to plus 1; ModalEngine::process at 0x1bd24 turns it into a frequency either as the filter frequency times 2 to the power of twice the offset, which is 24 semitones at the end of the knob, or as the filter frequency plus the offset times 500Hz, according to the unit switch, and the result is clamped to between 20Hz and 0.4899 of the sample rate. The switch defaults to semitones. A muted voice is skipped entirely. The five mute buttons are plain parameters used as latches, each with its own lamp. Nothing in the plugin reads a channel count, so every port is mono. The panel menu carries only Reload panel and Poll SVG for reload, which every module in this plugin has and which only reload the panel artwork.

WaveguideDelay.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.0.0 binary. The parameter the maker names Glitch, and the panel prints GLITCH, is read in exactly one place: WaveguideDelay::process at 0x267cc, the branch taken when the clock is absent or has stopped for more than two beats, where it becomes 0.02 times 100 to the power of the knob, that is 20ms to 2 seconds of base delay time. It has no other effect anywhere in the function, so with a clock patched the knob, its attenuverter and its CV jack are all dead. Grain Shift Delay, which is built the same way, takes that base time from a Base time menu item instead, so this looks like a knob that was repurposed and never relabelled. The thirteen grid ratios are the floats at 0x38660, 8 down to 1/512. The delay is clamped to between 2 samples and four seconds. Tone runs 0 to 1 on the knob and is mapped to minus 1 to plus 1 before it reaches the damping filter in WGDelayEngine::stepBuffer at 0x26ffc. Feedback runs minus 0.95 to plus 0.95 with a default at the centre, so the module starts with no repeats. Delay units is a menu item with no panel control, and has no widget position, so it gets no tag. Nothing in the plugin reads a channel count, so every port is mono. The panel menu also carries Reload panel and Poll SVG for reload, which every module in this plugin has and which only reload the panel artwork; they are left out.

GrainShiftDelay.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.0.0 binary. The nine note values are the floats at 0x36200, 8 beats down to a thirty-second of one, displayed by DivParamQuantity as 2/1 through 1/128. Scatter sets the grain launch spacing to the grain length divided by two times 4 to the power of the knob, and the random throw to 0.18 of a second times the knob. The frequency shift is the knob in semitones divided by 12 and multiplied by the Max shift figure, so the marking in semitones is a scale on a linear shift rather than a transposition. The four menu figures start at 50ms grain, 0.5 seconds base time, 20ms crossfade and 1000Hz maximum shift, which are the constants at 0x36150. There is a tenth parameter, index 4, that the maker calls Feel: GrainShift::process at 0x12770 reads it and multiplies the delay by 2/3 for Triplet or 1.5 for Dotted, but neither panel SVG carries the feel-switch element the widget looks for and the context menu does not offer it, so it has no widget position, cannot be clicked or turned, and is stuck on Straight. It gets no line and no tag. The sumRange spelling of the feedback clamp is written as a voltage because the field takes no other shape; the quantity itself is a gain, not a voltage. Nothing in the plugin reads a channel count, so every port is mono. The panel menu also carries Reload panel and Poll SVG for reload, which every module in this plugin has and which only reload the panel artwork; they are left out.

lines: A clock-synced generative LFO: two sine phasors beat against each other to make a slow envelope, and an I Ching change engine keeps moving the rate, the depth of the beating and the phase between them

Sets how far the two phasors cancel: at 0% the envelope is flat and at 100% the beat falls to a full null once each cycle
Sets the phase offset between the two phasors, 0 to 360 degrees, which shifts where in the cycle the envelope's dip falls
Sets the chance, on each beat, that the change engine takes a step; at 0% nothing ever changes and at 100% a step falls on every beat, eight of them carrying one trigram line across and flipping it
Chooses the shape of the internal modulator that the change engine steers the rate, the symmetry and the phase with: sine, triangle, saw or square
Multiplies or divides the clock to set the internal modulator's rate, in the same fourteen steps the beat rate offers; the module starts at the clock rate itself
A clock here sets the beat everything in the module is measured against, taken from rising edges above 1V; with nothing patched the module runs from an internal beat of 2Hz
A rising edge above 1V glides both phasors back to the start of their cycles by the shorter way round, rather than jumping them
The beating envelope, 0V to 10V or -5V to +5V according to the menu, despite this being the jack the panel prints GATE
A 1ms pulse at 10V at the start of every beat cycle, despite this being the jack the panel prints CV

Menu — CV OUT range: 0 V – 10 V, -5 V – +5 V — sets whether the envelope output swings from zero upwards or around zero

Yao.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.0.0 binary. The two output jacks are printed the wrong way round. Yao::process writes the envelope to outputs[0] at 0x2c35c and the pulse to outputs[1] at 0x2c380, and the maker's own port names agree, calling them Envelope CV and Beat gate. The widget binds outputs[0] to the SVG element named cv and outputs[1] to the one named gate, but the two panel files disagree about where those elements are: in Yao.svg the circle named gate is at x 112.83 and cv at 158.5, while in Yao-dark.svg they are the other way round, and no other panel in the plugin has such a mismatch. SvgHelper::findNamed searches whichever theme's file is loaded, so which physical hole carries which signal depends on the theme the module was created under. The scanned positions here are from a dark-theme Rack, where outputs[0], the envelope, is the left jack, under the lettering GATE, and outputs[1], the pulse, is the right one under CV. In the light theme they land the other way round and the lettering is then correct. The lettering itself sits at the same place in both files. Somebody should tell the maker. The fourteen clock ratios are printed by the RatioQuantity as /8, /6, /4, /3, /2, then multiplications by 2/3, 3/4, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8, with the default at index 7, which is times 1. The change engine, Yao::changeTick at 0x2c878, draws a random number each beat and does nothing unless it falls below the Mutability knob; otherwise it moves one of three depth values by 0.125 towards 0 or 1 depending on the matching trigram bit, and when a depth reaches its end that bit flips and one of the other two lines is chosen at random. The three depths modulate the beat rate as a power of two, the symmetry and the phase. The beat frequency is clamped to 50Hz and the clock period to a floor of two samples. Nothing in the plugin reads a channel count, so every port is mono. The panel menu also carries Reload panel and Poll SVG for reload, which every module in this plugin has and which only reload the panel artwork; they are left out.
